snippet.title: How to do Line Integrals!
snippet.description:
Line integrals are SUPER useful in physics and engineering! And are also a cool math technique for adding up little bits of stuff along a path. But beware! The path you take will change how much stuff you get along the way, so let's look at an example problem to help us understand (and calculate) a simple line integral!

snippet.title: Get through the pandemic with making!
snippet.description:
I love the maker movement for many reasons, two of which are very relevant as we all cope with the chaos and disruption of this pandemic:
1. making and creating are good for our bodies, minds, and souls, and
2. an entrepreneurial spirit can help fill in income gaps.
For project ideas and learning, here are some sites I suggest:
➡️ www.foxbotindustries.com (arts-based STEM projects for beginners to intermediate++, vetted content)
➡️ www.instructables.com (wide variety of projects for all types, content not vetted)
➡️www.hackster.io (intermediate and advanced electronics and coding, content not vetted)
➡️www.adafruit.com (beginner to advanced electronics and coding, vetted content)
➡️www.sparkfun.com (beginner to advanced electronics and coding, vetted content)
➡️aka.ms/hackingSTEM (project based educational curriculum)

please share resources with your community and feel free to post things here!

we will get through this together 💖💖💖
remember: be kind, love yourself and others, and always do your best (and your best is variable, so it may be different now than during not-pandemic).

snippet.title: What the heck is exponential growth?
snippet.description:
What is exponential growth and what does it look like?? Let's learn about it by comparing it to the "smiley graph", aka a parabola aka the x squared graph!
Why does exponential growth matter? Because it is a helpful model that crops up in population growth and in things like this pandemic we are all dealing with right now. Knowing what it means helps us make more reasonable, informed decisions so we can protect ourselves and our loved ones.

P.S. e = 2.72 (or 2.71828...)  :)

snippet.title: Intro to Solving Differential Equations! (Part 2/2)
snippet.description:
In this part, we'll tackle two second-order (aka second derivative) differential equations! The first example we'll pull from a physics problem (classic object-falling sort of shenanigans) to see how we solve a separable second order diff. eqn., and in the second example we'll tackle a harder example but pull from past mathematicians work to make our lives easier, yay!

snippet.title: Intro to Solving Differential Equations! (Part 1/2)
snippet.description:
